steps.text: I'm June, Maya's aunt. Her birthday is this week and I want to give her $300. Should I just send her the cash? She's on SSI, and her family made a Giftwise page for her: maya.

Gift page for Maya (/g/maya). Open needs: Wheelchair repair: $420 still needed, paid to Riverside Mobility Repair; Laptop for college: $649 still needed, paid to Eastgate College Bookstore; Electric bill, this month: $138 still needed, paid to Maya's ABLE account; Therapy co-pay: $90 still needed, paid to Northside Physical Therapy. Any amount can also go to her ABLE account.

Cash counts as income. $300 minus $80 in exclusions leaves $220 counted in November, so their January check would be $809. Giving the item itself keeps $1,029. Sources: 20 CFR 416.1121: types of unearned income, including gifts; POMS SI 00830.520: Gifts; POMS SI 00810.410: Infrequent or Irregular Income Exclusion; POMS SI 00810.420: $20 General Income Exclusion; POMS SI 02005.001: Retrospective monthly accounting.
$300 for Maya: $300 to Riverside Mobility Repair (Wheelchair repair). Her check stays $1,029. Given as cash, it would be $809.

Hi June, what a kind gift. Before you send it, here's what I found.

**If you send $300 in cash:** Social Security counts cash gifts as income. They let her keep the first $80, so $220 would count against her. That would lower her monthly check from $1,029 to $809, so she'd get $220 less. Because of how Social Security does its timing, the lower check would land two months after the gift. None of that money goes to Social Security; it just comes off her check.

**What I suggest instead:** Maya's family made her a gift page, and the biggest thing on it is a $420 wheelchair repair. Giftwise would pay all $300 straight to Riverside Mobility Repair. Since the money goes to the repair shop and not to Maya, her check stays at $1,029.

If you'd like to pick something else, these are also on her page:
- Laptop for college ($649)
- Physical therapy co-pay ($90)
- Money for her ABLE account (a special savings account that doesn't affect her benefits)

Do you want to go ahead with $300 for the wheelchair repair? Once you say yes, I'll set up a PayPal checkout and send you the link. Nothing gets charged until you approve it in PayPal yourself.
That makes sense. Yes, please set up the $300 that way.

PayPal checkout ready for $300 to Maya, paid to 1 recipient. The person giving should open this link and approve in PayPal: [PayPal approval link]. After they approve, the receipt will be at /r/[receipt].

Your checkout is ready, June. Open this link and approve the payment in PayPal:

[PayPal approval link]

PayPal's own record shows one payment of $300.00 for Maya's wheelchair repair, and it hasn't been paid yet: it's waiting for you to approve it.

If you sent the $300 as cash, her monthly check would drop from $1,029 to $809. Paid straight to the repair shop like this, it stays at $1,029.

After you approve, your receipt will be at /r/[receipt]. This is a test version of PayPal, so no real money will move. Happy birthday to Maya.
